newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian cargo plane crashes in Siberia, 23 die.
newsitem.headline: Russian cargo plane crashes in Siberia, 23 die.

text.p: A military cargo plane delivering food to the Russian Far East has crashed in Siberia, killing all 23 people on board, officials said on Thursday.

A spokesman for the Ministry for Emergency Services said 10 crew members and 13 passengers died when the Ilyushin Il-76 came down on Wednesday night, shortly after take-off from the southern Siberian city of Abakan.
It was the lastest in a series of accidents involving the ungainly transport jet, distinguished by the drooping wings above its fuselage and a bulbous glass nose-cone.
A Kazakh-registered Il-76 was involved in the world's worst mid-air collision with a Saudi jumbo jet near Delhi on November 12.
The head of the Russian air force press office said the plane which crashed on Wednesday had been delivering 30 tonnes of food to the Far Eastern Kamchatka peninsula.

"The Russian government has asked military transport planes to make more then 120 flights to the Far East to deliver food because civilian organisations were too short of money to deliver goods this summer by ship," Gennady Lisenkov said.
"The air forces began such flights a month ago."
Lisenkov said it appeared that the plane had crashed into the side of a hill. The causes of the accident were being investigated.
The Il-76, designed as a military tank transporter, is a mainstay of Russia's armed forces and of its commercial fleet.
It has become a familiar sight on the world's freight routes since the collapse of the Soviet Union.

Last April, an Il-76 came down on Kamchatka, killing all aboard. One came down near Belgrade in August, killing 10 crewmen and a Ukrainian crew died when their Il-76 crashed on take-off at Kinshasa in June.
A surge in air accidents in Russia in the past few years has been blamed on financial difficulties, which have led to poor maintenance standards and placed extra pressure on crews.
Interfax news agency said 19 bodies had so far been recovered from the wreckage of the latest crash and all four black boxes had been recovered.
The four-engined plane had disappeared from radar screens just seven minutes after take-off, although it took several hours for the authorities to confirm that it had crashed.
